title: ‘Worst decision in history’: Guardian readers shaken and stirred by the casting of Robert Pattinson as Bond
text:
So it’s official, Robert Pattinson will be James Bond. The long-awaited announcement of who would be stepping into 007’s tuxedo came as a surprise, and has divided opinion, judging by the more than 700 responses the Guardian received to a callout on the topic.
Readers were split on whether bosses at the franchise’s owner Amazon were right to give the role to the star of Twilight, Tenet and The Batman. Here are some of their views.
‘Deliciously dark’
Brilliant casting! And with Denis Villeneuve directing, I’m expecting something deliciously dark. Pattinson has that perfect “is he a good guy or a bad guy?” face. There’s something mysterious and slightly sinister about him. Definitely not Austin Powers. I’m absolutely thrilled and applaud this direction for Bond. Tatara, US
‘Robert has something extra’
His face is such that it always adds some mysterious vibe to whatever he is expressing as an actor. I do think this will add more depth to the Bond character. The other candidates were more within the predictable bubble, Robert has something extra beyond that and hopefully it will deliver high quality to the next Bond films. Well done! Kris, the Netherlands
‘This is an abomination’
I have never felt this much rage in my life. This is the worst decision in all of cinema history. Since the age of five I’ve been watching James Bond. I have seen every film four, maybe even five times. Never in my life have I been more disappointed by a casting decision. This is an abomination. Robert Pattinson does not have a good appearance for the role. He lacks the heroic, flirtatious, life on the edge aesthetic. In my opinion, he is is also simply not sexy enough to be a Bond. He should have been a villain, that I would watch. Gemma, Australia
‘They missed the mark’
Casting Pattinson as Bond is a huge letdown. It feels like a lazy, play-it-safe studio decision lacking any real depth or vision. They missed the mark entirely – this goes against everything that defines the character of Bond. Nemanja, 34, Bosnia and Herzegovina
‘Villeneuve and Pattinson is a dream come true’
I was delighted to hear about Pattinson’s casting. I am a long-time fan of Bond; my mother took me to see Skyfall in the cinema when I was 10 (I think she had a bit of a crush on Daniel Craig). My favourite Bond is Timothy Dalton, I think Pattinson could bring the same dark intensity to the role. My favourite director is Denis Villeneuve, and Pattinson is one of my favourite actors, to have them working together on the next Bond film feels like a dream come true. Joe, 24, Brighton
‘He has been in every movie under the sun’
Boring! Don’t get me wrong, I’m sure Robert Pattinson will be amazing in the role but he has been in every movie under the sun the past couple of years and it would just be nice to see someone else’s face on the screen and given a chance. I was really rooting for Nicholas Hoult. Rebecca, 26, London
‘Unpredictability and a faintly dangerous charm’
Many of us assumed the next Bond would be a fresh-faced actor in his late 20s. Pattinson is 40, so the tone shift isn’t about youth. That may be a strength. A 40-year-old Pattinson can be seasoned and unsettling without being a young boy playing at being a killer. Where Craig’s Bond was a blunt instrument with a broken heart, Pattinson brings something stranger: unpredictability and a faintly dangerous charm. Villeneuve clearly sees something similar. The two have already worked together, and Pattinson plays the villain Scytale in Dune: Part Three. If Villeneuve can make Bond as immersive and unnerving as Arrakis, we’re in for something special. Jayjay, London
‘It’s weird to see Batman as Bond’
I don’t like it simply because it’s so weird as a movie lover to see Batman as Bond. I know actors obviously take different roles but two iconic characters in the same timeframe! Is there really such a lack of talented actors who can perform in Hollywood? Josh, teacher, 33, Sheffield
‘Too old for a reset role’
This is a missed opportunity. Pattinson is a good actor but too established in other roles. Also, too old for a reset role. A grave miscalculation. Bond has always been most successful when the actor has been a blank slate on whom the audience can project its fantasies of Bond. Pattinson is too established. I also wonder whether he can bring the necessary camp touch – the knowing, self-referential, theatrical excess. Martin, lawyer, Bordeaux, France
‘I am intrigued to see what he can bring’
My initial reaction wasn’t especially positive. R-Patz, Bond? Cedric Diggory from Harry Potter, the Twilight pin-up, a Batman?! I thought he was too well known to mould himself into 007. It felt like a dramatic and high-profile curveball. But perhaps that’s why it makes perfect sense. I had been rooting for Jack Lowden, but Pattinson has proven in recent times how good an actor he is – I am now intrigued to see what he can bring to the famous character. The casting will undoubtedly draw a lot of attention and scrutiny, and put bums on seats for his films. Davy, tour guide, 32, Perthshire
